facts.value: QTEM (Quantitative Techniques for Economics and Management) is a growing international network of leading universities worldwide, supported by international business partners. The department's business partner in the QTEM network is Banco Santander.
The QTEM program includes one or two semesters abroad and an internship.
Track 1: 1 semester abroad + an internship of 240 hours; Track 2: 2 semesters abroad + an internship of 240 hours.

All QTEM students participate in the QTEM Global Business Analytics Challenge (GBAC), which consists of group work on a business case and two preparatory courses that teach soft skills necessary for successful teamwork and case resolution.
A total of 50 ECTS credits must be earned in quantitative courses, with 22 ECTS credits each semester at one of the QTEM partner universities.
The master's thesis is written at the home university in Frankfurt.
Upon successful completion of the QTEM program and the master's program of the department, students receive the master's degree from the department and a QTEM certificate.
A mandatory requirement for participation in the QTEM program is proof of a GMAT test result of at least 555 points or an equivalent GRE score.
An equivalent GRE score (e.g., 155 in Verbal Reasoning and 159 in Quantitative Reasoning) can also be accepted.
A new GMAT test format will be introduced starting from the fourth quarter of 2024, requiring a minimum score of 600.
The QTEM exchange takes place in the 3rd and/or 4th semester.

Students in the first semester of the master's programs Business Administration (BWL), Management Science (Mgmt Sc.), Money, Macro and Finance (MMF), and International Economics and Economic Policy (MIEEP) can apply.
The application deadline for the 2026/27 academic year is February 1, 2026.
New announcements are published in late October each year, with the application deadline being February 1 of the following year.
